I know state tree provides state root and Merkle proofs, then why do we need state db, use just state tree all the time? It seems your question is: **If we have a trie/tree why do we also need a database?** If you have a **trie data structure**, you will also need a **storage layer** to store the original data and also any intermediate data that the trie may produce such as hashes. The storage layer could be in-memory or it could be persistent like rocksdb or leveldb. The trie is able to access the storage layer in order to do operations such as make merkle proofs, compute/update the state root. Sometimes implementations do duplicate data by creating two storage layers. One is persistent and could be rocksdb/leveldb. The other is in-memory and is referred to as a cache. excerpts.content:
A basic question. Why do we need two things - state tree (Merkle Patricia Trie) and a state db (rocksdb / leveldb)? Isn't data duplicated? 

I know state tree provides state root and Merkle proofs, then why do we need state db, use just state tree all the time?

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
It seems your question is: **If we have a trie/tree why do we also need a database?**

If you have a **trie data structure**, you will also need a **storage layer** to store the original data and also any intermediate data that the trie may produce such as hashes.

The storage layer could be in-memory or it could be persistent like rocksdb or leveldb.

The trie is able to access the storage layer in order to do operations such as make merkle proofs, compute/update the state root. 

Sometimes implementations do duplicate data by creating two storage layers. One is persistent and could be rocksdb/leveldb. The other is in-memory and is referred to as a cache. The cache is much faster to access, so you put commonly retrieved items in it to make trie operations faster.

(This is in general, I don't know how it works exactly in Ethereum)

Suppose we do not need Merkle roots for some reason, then is rocksdb not enough?

Suppose also that I take care of cache. Then do I need state tree at all? I can work on rocksdb directly. It too provides efficient read and write accesses

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Yeah exactly, if you don’t need to create merkle proofs or a merkle root, then you could store the data directly in a key value database.

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: You will still be able to verify merkle proofs given a root, but you would need to get the root from some trusted source
